title: Review & Iterate Ads
description: Find what to fix in a draft, learn from a batch, or plan a clean variation of an existing ad.

modes.title: Review one ad
modes.description: Use an ad image, script, video frames, or results to get specific revisions.

steps.title: Inspect the creative
steps.instruction: Identify the source asset and its intended buyer, offer, and action. Audit the opening, reading path, promise, mechanism, proof, and CTA in source order. Cite an exact line, frame or timestamp, or visible image location for each observation. Where a product research record or brief is supplied, compare against its locked desire, angle, claims and evidence IDs. List missing inputs and separate what the ad shows from your interpretation. Pinpoint the first buyer decision that the creative leaves unresolved. Anchor it to a visible or quoted cue, name the live objection it triggers and explain which kind of proof would answer it. A click or an opinion about the design alone cannot establish that buyers believe the claim.
checks: Creative observations are anchored to an inspected asset, with unavailable portions clearly marked.
The ad's message and each consequential claim are checked against available product evidence and the intended CTA.
The review distinguishes visible or written facts from hypotheses about how a buyer might react.

steps.title: Prioritize revisions
steps.instruction: Use the inspected asset and findings to give up to three prioritized edits, each with its affected line, shot or image element, a specific replacement, and the expected buyer or creative effect. If results were supplied, check the asset match, comparable exposure, reporting window and KPI before using them. Identify one next test or edit and the evidence that would support it.
checks: Each revision includes actionable replacement copy or a concrete visual change grounded in the prior audit.
Creative critique and measured results are separate, with any weak or unavailable performance evidence labeled.
The recommended first change preserves the selected offer, angle, and substantiated product claims unless the brief explicitly requests a change.

modes.title: Diagnose an underperforming ad
modes.description: Compare the ad, funnel and results, then choose one test that could explain the miss.

steps.title: Align the ad, destination and results
steps.instruction: Build a source-linked evidence table covering the exact creative and promise, the product and offer, the landing page and checkout, and the supplied delivery and purchase data. Reconcile creative ID, destination version, market, spend, dates, units, and metric and attribution definitions. Compare with a relevant control, target or historical period only when comparable. Keep attributed purchases separate from first-time customer counts. Distinguish low or interrupted delivery from conversion weakness. A blank value, absent placement or uninspected checkout is unknown. Never convert a gap into zero or assume an ad underperformed from unequal delivery alone. If data is sparse or no baseline exists, retain the available observations and state what is needed to classify performance.
checks: Every material fact or metric traces to the supplied asset, export or page, and missing and incomparable inputs are explicit.
The review separates exposure, attributed purchases and first-time customers, and it names any gaps that block a performance conclusion.

steps.title: Rank likely causes of the miss
steps.instruction: Use the reconciled evidence to consider delivery and measurement, creative, product or offer, landing-page continuity, and checkout. Shortlist up to three plausible causes. For each, cite the strongest observation with an exact line, image region, destination section or metric, name a competing explanation, and say what evidence would change the ranking. A high CTR or low hold rate can generate a hypothesis about the opener or buyer fit; neither alone establishes the cause of weak acquisition. If landing-page or checkout evidence is materially stronger than creative evidence, route the recommendation there. When the evidence is inconclusive, state the next observation needed before picking a fix. For two plausible explanations that predict the same surface metric, identify the next observation that would distinguish them. Trace the break through comparable exposed, landing, checkout and paid populations when supplied. Put reproducible factual or checkout defects ahead of speculative copy changes. If comparable video counts are supplied, separate three-second plays per impression, ThruPlays per impression, and ThruPlays per three-second play. Use the conditional rate to locate a possible breakdown after the opening. Account for video length and the completion rule.
checks: The ranking checks plausible funnel alternatives, distinguishes observed defects from causality, and gives concrete evidence and a disconfirming check for the leading explanation.
The recommended direction targets the strongest evidence, or requests a named missing observation when the source of underperformance remains unclear.
When video counts are available, attention rates identify their denominators and any material length or event mismatch. A missing comparison remains open.

steps.title: Choose one next test
steps.instruction: Turn the leading viable explanation into one controlled change, or specify one evidence-collection step when the diagnosis is inconclusive. Name the exact before and after, owner, creative and destination IDs, input held fixed, main outcome and guardrail, and what result would support, weaken or leave the explanation unresolved. Use comparable purchase or acquisition outcomes where available; identify attention signals as secondary diagnostics. Use a supplied profit or CPA threshold only with a matching measurement basis; leave numeric thresholds open if inputs are missing. If a page or checkout fix is selected, retain the ad as the control and include a handoff for Store Review & CRO.
checks: The output specifies one testable change or one concrete evidence request, and it links directly to the evidence and uncertainty from the diagnosis.
The plan names constants, metric definitions and a decision rule. It avoids invented economics, target values or results.

modes.title: Review a finished ad before launch
modes.description: Check the actual ad image or timecoded video frames against the approved brief.

steps.title: Check the finished export against its brief
steps.instruction: Identify the supplied final asset and version and the approved brief. Use an attached final PNG, JPG or WebP, or attached timecoded frames and supplied transcript for video. A script, slot map, storyboard or brief is preparation evidence. Treat a missing inspectable final asset as a blocker and request the export or representative timecoded frames. Cite the exact image area or supplied timecode for every finding. Check opening and next beat, what the eye sees at feed size, legibility and typos, correct product and use, whether visuals and copy communicate the same desire and supported benefit, claim and offer continuity, brand requirements, and what the CTA asks the viewer to do. For video, inspect captions, timing or audio only when the supplied evidence supports each judgment. Score pacing against comprehension for the chosen format. Mark uninspected aspects and missing proof or brief fields. Return a readiness decision scoped to what you could inspect, with any launch-blocking finding and one specific fix or input for each. Do not offer a performance prediction or launch anything. For a proposed blocker, identify whether it violates an approved requirement, materially changes what buyers could infer, or is an optional editorial preference. A different acceptable CTA wording or suggested headline alone cannot justify holding the export.
checks: The report identifies the actual inspected asset and version, and findings are tied to observable locations or timecodes. If the final asset cannot be inspected, the result is blocked.
The review checks product use, legibility and message and offer continuity where supported, and identifies exactly which footage, audio, brief fields or proofs remain unavailable.
Readiness is scoped to the actual evidence. Each launch-blocking issue has a concrete fix or required input.

For each copy or CTA mismatch, check the item's own label and the current brief. A proposed line remains optional even under a heading such as 'copy lock'. A wording change alone blocks launch only when that wording was explicitly required. Report other differences as editorial decisions unless there is a separate evidenced defect.

modes.title: Review a weekly batch
modes.description: Use creative assets and their performance export to decide what to repeat, revise, or test next.

steps.title: Match assets to their results
steps.instruction: Use the bundled creative-review method and consult the original Weekly Creative Review when available. Verify fidelity against an original when expressly requested. Reconcile each reporting row to the actual creative ID and inspected asset. Capture the period, spend, exposure, volume, attribution context, KPI target, and comparator as supplied. Label unmatched or incomparable records. If you report blended rates, compute them from totals and show the numerator and denominator. For Evolve creative outcome labels, choose the rule by monthly ad spend and identify its source/version. Reconcile the first-week numerator, denominator and comparable-week growth at the rule’s scope: the originating campaign in initial-campaign tiers, or the whole account in the high-spend account tier. Apply the agreed KPI and allocation method. Disclose a decision-changing conflict across source versions. A small-sample example with an unset cutoff supplies no qualifying rule. Treat examples from other tiers and forced ad-set allocation separately. If inputs are missing, identify which outcome branches remain possible. A missing scale series only affects a high-share ad’s final label. Distinguish actual spend from configured budget. State provisional conditions in the headline and detailed findings.
checks: The batch table preserves creative IDs and comparison context, including gaps and unmatched rows.
Calculated blended metrics use summed numerators and denominators, with undefined values labeled.
Winner language is supported by the relevant decision criteria and measured inputs, or the outcome is uncertain.

Each material outcome uses the applicable share, KPI and scale evidence for its branch, at the benchmark’s period and campaign/account scope. Source-version disagreements that change the decision are explicit. A consistently provisional or open decision names the missing comparison and a revisit condition.

steps.title: Diagnose patterns in the batch
steps.instruction: Compare aligned results and actual assets. Identify patterns in angle, hook, demonstration, proof, or format using asset IDs and exact observations. Separate attention measures from purchase outcomes and identify reasonable alternative explanations. Apply Evolve outcome criteria only where the criteria and necessary inputs are accessible. Recommend the next test that would distinguish the strongest explanations. Check whether audience, placement or returning-buyer mix could reverse the apparent ordering. When counts are available, calculate per-segment rates on like denominators and state the weights for any fixed-mix comparison. Keep the blended observation, the within-segment evidence and the cause distinct. Distinguish a hook that earns clicks from a promise whose landing experience earns purchases. Where a brief and the actual ad are supplied, compare intended buyer, desire and opening awareness against the first in-ad cue, then locate the belief or proof asked of the buyer in the body. Use the operator’s observations as attributed hypotheses.
checks: Each learning links to specific creatives, results and the context that makes the comparison meaningful.
The analysis separates observations, possible causes and the evidence that would disconfirm them.
The next test targets a named uncertainty and preserves essential comparison conditions.
If mix differs, the readout uses comparable segments and denominators and explains any reversal of the blended ranking.
When the plan and ad are both available, the diagnosis compares the intended element to an observed line or frame. With less evidence, identify the comparison that remains open.

steps.title: Rank the next briefs
steps.instruction: Convert the batch findings into a ranked queue of next briefs. For each, give the parent creative ID when available, objective, specific change, locked elements, required assets, primary KPI, and source result or unresolved dependency. Use the existing Evolve roadmap. Where prior briefs or ads show it, group related variants under their underlying buyer, desire, angle and benefit. Show which creative decisions the batch actually varied. Identify a materially different concept as an exploratory option only when evidence supports it and the task calls for broader exploration. Treat a multi-element concept as a package result. Return the next production decision. If delivery mix drives the apparent winner, propose a same-segment controlled comparison, specifying who is eligible, what stays fixed, the primary business outcome and when a decision can be made. Do not label an unrandomized fixed-mix comparison causal. Only classify a next brief as a winner-derived iteration for a substantiated Spend Winner or Breakthrough. For a KPI Winner or Loser, record the learning and a diagnostic next observation. Distinguish any explicitly requested exploratory redesign.
checks: Every ranked brief traces to a batch observation or to a clearly labeled exploratory hypothesis.
The queue preserves creative IDs, required assets, the measurement plan and dependencies. When concept history is available, it distinguishes variants from new ideas.
The queue distinguishes an eligible winner iteration from a diagnostic action or an explicitly scoped exploratory test.

modes.title: Plan a variation
modes.description: Use one parent ad to create a controlled next test.

steps.title: Verify the parent ad
steps.instruction: Identify the parent creative ID, version where available, and exact original creative element to change. A supplied ID and faithful text or transcript can support a text-only proposal. Mark the image and any unchanged copy that you could not inspect as unverified; require the original file if the proposed change depends on inspecting it. Align any measurements to the stated parent, period, KPI, spend, conversion volume and comparator. State the locked buyer, angle, offer facts and what remains fixed. Label the project exploratory if available measurements are insufficient to establish a winner. Check the parent promise and depiction against current product facts before reusing its wording. If the historical control promises something unverified, preserve it in the retrospective record and design a substantiated control for the next live test. For a retrospective or text-only decision, record missing buyer or offer fields and the concrete confirmation required before reuse. Deliver the historical decision with the proposed control explicitly conditional; do not invent missing locks or mark the control launch-ready. Before authorizing a winner-derived child, establish the applicable Evolve outcome from the matching ad spend, tier-specific campaign or account denominator, KPI and scale evidence, or retain a supplied outcome with clear provenance and limits. Record what the actual hook asks the buyer to recognize, and the proof or belief the body needs. Handoff either winner iteration (Spend Winner or Breakthrough), learning only (KPI Winner or Loser), or an explicitly requested exploratory test. Unknown status cannot substantiate a winner.
checks: The parent and the exact element to change are tied to inspected or explicitly supplied evidence. For a text-only proposal, an exact supplied text and parent ID suffice; any uninspected files and unchanged elements are clearly marked.
The supported outcome or exploratory status is explicit and grounded in the available measurements.

The buyer, angle, offer and fixed elements are sourced and locked wherever supplied. For a bounded historical or text-only decision, missing locks, their effect on readiness and the exact confirmation needed for reuse are explicit. A control described as ready for live use must have all material locks.

The handoff states the eligible route and the evidence behind it. A learning-only decision is a complete result for an ineligible parent. A request to iterate a winner alone is insufficient to override eligibility.

steps.title: Draft one testable change
steps.instruction: Apply the bundled iteration method to this parent. Consult the original Ten-Step process and Iteration Brief when available. Assess original-source fidelity only if the user expressly asks for it; the bundled method is sufficient for an ordinary variation. Choose one material change and write a variation with a specific hypothesis. Identify parent and child IDs, show the exact original and replacement, name the elements held fixed, and retain the evidence IDs for claims. A larger requested swing should be labeled a package comparison with each changed element listed. Honor the parent decision. For a learning-only route, return the observed weakness, competing explanation and next observation, with no child creative. When no parent decision was supplied, check the evidence or explicit exploratory scope before drafting.
checks: For an eligible or explicitly exploratory child, the draft shows the exact change and its control. For a learning-only parent it returns a specific diagnosis and withholds a child.
A proposed child identifies the isolated variable and fixed cues. A diagnostic-only report identifies the evidence that could change the decision.
Material claims retain their evidence limits, and the output labels its eligibility and status consistently with the parent decision.

steps.title: Plan the comparison
steps.instruction: Write a reusable Evolve experiment card with the parent and child IDs, test unit, assignment conditions, primary KPI, guardrail, observation window, tracking and decision rule. Use supplied baseline and traffic to justify thresholds when available. Define an inconclusive result and leave missing numeric conditions open. Provide a result-log entry for the eventual reading. A learning-only handoff ends with a record of the current result, the next discriminating observation and the condition for reconsideration. Keep it separate from a child experiment. If this stage runs alone, distinguish a substantiated parent from a requested exploratory comparison.
checks: A proposed experiment defines the control, change, KPI and decision rule. A learning-only handoff instead defines the observation and condition that could reopen the parent.
Any proposed comparison preserves audience, placement, destination and offer, or records the material confounds.
Thresholds use supplied economics or an applicable account benchmark. Unavailable evidence and provisional status are explicit.

title: Store Review & CRO
description: Improve a store's copy, product images and path to purchase, or write a page that delivers on an ad's promise.

modes.title: Review store content and images
modes.description: Start from a store URL, screenshots, gallery images, copy, or analytics.

steps.title: Inspect the page and gallery
steps.instruction: Start with the supplied storefront, target buyer, traffic source and conversion action. Inspect mobile first at roughly 390 pixels where feasible and compare desktop if provided or accessible. Record exactly which page sections, slides, viewport and purchase states could be inspected. Check first-screen promise, offer, proof, gallery roles and readability, variants, shipping and returns, CTA, and purchase friction. Use research evidence or label the gap. Offer a keep, move, improve or replace decision for each consequential inspected gallery image.
checks: Each visual or mobile finding cites a screenshot, section, slide or accessible viewport, with the scope and gaps stated.
The audit covers the first screen, purchasing offer, images and next action to the extent those are observable.
Findings separate observed blockers from hypotheses about shopper reaction and cite any supplied metric context.

steps.title: Prioritize fixes and choose one test
steps.instruction: Use the inspected findings to deliver up to three ranked changes with exact replacement copy, a revised gallery order or an image brief where relevant, and the buyer question each fix answers. Use only verified terms and approved product proof. Choose the first controlled test with its section, current version, proposed change, primary metric, guardrail and any interim evidence or traffic it needs. Return draft materials for owner review. Classify confirmed wrong prices, broken actions and invented terms as repairs. Validate the corrected path before testing an uncertain persuasion change. For that experiment define the eligible exposure, denominator and primary downstream action; missing baseline traffic or device data limits a lift estimate. If the supplied data cross ads with destinations, map the actual ad–page cells and compare destinations within the same creative. Identify unobserved pairs and optimized allocation. For a causal page test, use the same incoming ad and offer with random assignment of eligible arrivals.
checks: Every priority cites an audit observation and provides a concrete improvement or usable replacement.
New copy and gallery proposals use verified product facts, with precise placeholders for evidence gaps.
The first test isolates a named change and gives a primary metric and guardrail without promising uplift.
Confirmed defects have a verification path and are separated from hypotheses that justify an experiment.
For a destination comparison, the recommendation distinguishes an observed ad–page pairing from a page effect and states the assignment required for the latter.

modes.title: Write or rewrite a product page
modes.description: Turn product evidence and buyer objections into a mobile-friendly sales page.

steps.title: Map the buyer's questions
steps.instruction: Use the current page, product research and any supplied ad or brief to map the buyer's first question, desired outcome, offer, main objections, evidence and CTA. Identify which existing sections serve those jobs and which need revision. Keep the approved angle and terms fixed unless the user supplied new ones. Flag an unavailable page and proceed from approved product facts if they support a fresh draft. Track the exact incoming promise, the first page element that could confirm it and the evidence that qualifies it. Distinguish a verified demonstration on a particular surface or condition from a general product guarantee. Retain bundle contents, options and restrictions at the decision they affect.
checks: The message map traces the offer, claims, objections and proof to available sources.
Changes to existing copy are tied to inspected sections, and new sections have clear jobs.
Evidence gaps, conflicting terms and unverified claims are distinguished from approved inputs.

steps.title: Draft the page copy
steps.instruction: Draft the requested product-page sections in a mobile-first order, using the prior evidence map. Choose only the requested blocks. Put the primary action at the first supported buying decision. Add a mechanism, proof or FAQ only when it answers a real buyer question in those blocks. Call out which gallery image should support a claim where that matters. Keep pricing, variants, guarantees and shipping faithful to the source. Provide ready-to-paste text and keep verification notes separate. Make each critical condition legible alongside the line it qualifies. Describe the demonstration in ordinary shopper language and preserve its conditions. Keep editorial statements about evidence availability, gallery requests and proposed experiments in the owner notes. Give each block a distinct job and remove repeated contents or prices unless a later purchase decision requires them.
checks: The draft answers the buyer's main questions in a clear order with a readable first screen and CTA.
Claims and offer details are grounded in available evidence and placeholders are identified separately where needed.
Each requested section has usable copy and the draft preserves the selected angle and voice.

Material restrictions and demonstration conditions are legible to a shopper. Each requested block advances the purchase decision without duplicating a neighboring block or exposing internal verification commentary.

modes.title: Match an advertorial to an ad
modes.description: Carry the ad's hook, promise and proof through to a presell or landing page.

steps.title: Map the ad-to-page handoff
steps.instruction: Identify the version of the ad, its intended reader, the promise and question the hook opens, the evidence available, and the actual offer. Inspect the existing destination if supplied and accessible. Show where the first mobile screen resolves the ad's premise or introduces a disconnect, then map emotional and factual continuity from click through the CTA. Label any provisional interpretation when a source is missing.
checks: The handoff references the actual ad and any destination that was inspected.
Each gap specifies the affected buyer question, claim, evidence or offer term.
The map preserves the ad's locked reader, core message and substantiated promise.

steps.title: Draft the message-matched advertorial
steps.instruction: Turn the approved handoff into a mobile-scannable advertorial or revise the requested sections. Start by paying off the ad's opening question, then develop the mechanism, evidence, relevant objections, offer and CTA in order. Identify any needed imagery and disclosures. Cite product proof in verification notes and do not invent testimonials, studies, outcomes or offer terms. Make the brand or actual narrator identifiable. A customer quote, expert endorsement or apparently independent editorial voice needs an attributable source and the correct relationship; use an attributed demonstration or plain brand explanation when unavailable. Check that the closing offer, eligibility and action agree with the destination. Read the opening and proof section together. Set up the shopper’s situation or question in the opening, then show the concrete product action once in the proof beat. Use natural attribution such as first-person brand narration where accurate; keep source-ledger wording for the owner notes.
checks: The first screen fulfills the intended ad promise and the offer and CTA stay consistent through the page.
Copy is readable on mobile and evidence supports material statements, with explicit gaps for unavailable proof.
The draft separates ready-to-paste copy from asset, disclosure and verification notes.
The opening creates a reason to keep reading and the proof adds a concrete new observation. Repeating the demonstration or announcing internal documentation does not count as progression.

modes.title: Teardown a competitor page
modes.description: Learn from a reference page's structure, proof, copy roles and visual system.

steps.title: Map the reference page
steps.instruction: Use the supplied public page or screenshots. Inventory each inspectable section in order and describe its job, proof, mobile role and visual hierarchy. Identify reusable structure and section roles, then extract the target store's own visual references into a brand kit for future drafts if supplied. Record measured type and colors separately from estimates. Flag unspecified or inaccessible views and avoid unsupported conversion claims.
checks: The inventory covers each inspected section in order and says which screen or page areas were inaccessible.
Evidence distinguishes source claims, actual proof, and any hypotheses about section effectiveness.
The brand kit distinguishes verified measurements and own-brand choices from estimates or reference observations.

steps.title: Turn reference lessons into a test
steps.instruction: Translate useful reference structure into an original, evidence-backed suggestion for the user's store. Specify one section, the shopper problem it addresses, the brand-appropriate H1 or creative direction, and a test with control, variant, metric and guardrail. Use the user's style, product and proof instead of borrowing reference photos, testimonial copy, or identity assets. For every borrowed structural device, state the buyer question it answers and identify owned evidence that can answer it for this product. Omit or replace an unsupported proof slot rather than filling it with an invented review count, timer, certification or offer. Define the observable result that would change the recommendation. State the direction of that result. If an uncertainty interval is used for a proposed improvement, an upper bound below the minimum worthwhile gain weakens it; an interval entirely above that gain supports it. With insufficient observations, preserve the uncertainty.
checks: The recommendation ties to an inspected structural role and does not present a competitor's claims as product evidence.
The proposal uses original wording and appropriate brand direction, with unsupported items marked.
The test specifies one change, comparison conditions, a primary metric and a guardrail.
